chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the black dirhams that have images on them: Does a man pray while they are with him? He said, 'There is no harm with that if they are facing [away from the prayer direction].'

And al-Husayn ibn Sa'id said: I read a letter from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), asking him about praying in a garment whose filling is qazz (raw silk), so he wrote to him, 'I read it, there is no harm with praying in it.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh mentioned that the meaning in this report is the qazz of the goat, as opposed to the qazz of the silkworm.

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: Images or figures (of living beings) on objects
key_terms.مُوَارَاةً: Facing away (from the direction of prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray while wearing clothes with silk filling or carrying coins with images?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of minor impurities or distractions in prayer attire, specifically addressing coins with images (*tamasil*) and silk-filled garments. The ruling of 'no harm' (*la ba'sa*) for coins facing away highlights the Shia principle of ignoring negligible impurities in daily wear, while the distinction between goat silk (*qazz al-ma'iz*) and silkworm silk (*qazz al-ibrisam*) reflects the scholarly nuance in classifying permissible vs. prohibited silk for men.
